Manual and disjointed student internship administration in public sector establishments introduces record redundancy, attendance falsification, and delays in curriculum tracking and final clearance certificate issuance. This project presents the design and implementation of a robust, normalized relational database management system named
engineered to automate student IT internship management at the Lagos State Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology (MIST).
The conceptual model identified eight core entities: *Users* (operating strictly under two differentiated roles:

. The logical design was rigorously normalized to the Third Normal Form (3NF) to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies. Surrogate primary keys, composite unique keys, cascading referential integrity actions, and strict check/enum constraints were codified using MySQL 8.0 Data Definition Language (DDL).

The schema was programmatically mapped to a Node.js/Express application layer via the Sequelize Object-Relational Mapper (ORM), enabling indexed relational joins, atomic check-ins, automated 50/50 weighted coursework calculation, and digital completion validation. Comprehensive testing through MySQL CLI and API integration verified referential integrity enforcement, indexed query execution times under 20ms, and clean operational performance across all student and supervisor workflows.
Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS) constitute the structural backbone of modern organizational informatics. In professional training environments such as the
Lagos State Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology (MIST)

, dozens of university and polytechnic undergraduates are deployed annually under the Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme (SIWES). Interns are attached across diverse technical directorates—including Software Development, Cybersecurity, and Hardware & Network Engineering.

Managing student check-in compliance, progressive module completion, coursework submissions, and institutional certification through disparate paper logs or flat spreadsheets results in substantial data corruption, record duplication, and delayed verification. Applying formal relational database principles ensures ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) guarantees, enforces multi-table referential integrity, and provides secure concurrent access for administrative supervisors and student learners.
Prior to automation, SIWES management at MIST faced severe structural bottlenecks:
: Paper sign-in sheets allowed proxy attendance signing without timestamp validation or verification of intern physical presence within Alausa Secretariat.
: Practical resources and coursework tasks existed across ad-hoc file repositories without structured linkages to specific departmental tracks or enrolled students.
: Supervisors lacked unified queries to verify whether an intern satisfied both attendance criteria (minimum 3 check-ins per tenure week) and coursework submissions before signing clearance letters.
: Redundant administrative roles led to orphaned records and conflicting privileges.
The primary aim of this project is to model, design, and implement an enterprise-grade relational database (

CHAPTER TWO: DATABASE REQUIREMENTS AND CONCEPTUAL DESIGN

Field interviews and workflow observation at MIST revealed three critical functional actors: student interns, departmental supervisors, and executive directors. Analysis produced the following data storage requirements:
Interns must be identified by institutional email, tertiary matriculation number, phone contact, assigned unit, and variable SIWES duration (12, 24, or 52 weeks).
Daily check-ins must be restricted to one record per student per calendar date.
Curriculum materials must belong to specific units and modules, with persistent links to stored document assets.
Assignments require due date constraints, unit categorization, and student submission tracking.
Student performance requires an integrated metric reflecting module completions and assignment uploads.
Official clearance certificates require verification of full tenure attendance before generation.
Stores master records for all system actors. Role is strictly constrained to `'student'` or `'supervisor'`.
Holds curriculum resources published by supervisors.
Represents practical coursework assigned to an intern track.
Stores intern file deliverables and supervisor marks.
Tracks final completion review and certificate issuance.

LEFT JOIN submissions s ON a.id = s.assignment_id AND u.id = s.student_id

interns must log at least 3 daily check-ins for each week of their tenure

The empirical test data confirms that

meets all institutional specifications. Removing obsolete administrative roles simplified the schema structure, eliminated permission ambiguities, and ensured clean database state transitions. Automated cascade rules eliminated orphaned child rows, while strict composite keys prevented multiple daily check-ins and duplicate task submissions.

A robust relational database was designed and implemented for the MIST Student IT Portal. Conceptual modeling, 3NF normalization, and declarative schema constraints produced an efficient relational structure in MySQL. Integration with an Express/Sequelize application layer validated that academic and operational records can be accurately stored, processed, and retrieved with low latency and complete referential safety.
The database currently runs on a single primary MySQL node without automated read-replica distribution.
